title: Embedding-Space Orthogonal Decomposition for Robust Social Recommendation

problem.claim: Mismatched social ties can contaminate user representations and harm the robustness of graph-based social recommendation models.

gap.claim: Using a single weight for each social connection cannot selectively suppress misaligned components within an aggregated social message.

contributions.claim: ODSR orthogonally decomposes the aggregated social message into an aligned component and an orthogonal deviation, then uses a dimension-wise vector gate to regulate the deviation under ranking supervision.
ODSR introduces a contrastive regularizer that perturbs representations along deviation directions to improve robustness against imperfect social signals.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three datasets reportedly show that ODSR consistently outperforms strong baselines.
Additional analyses reportedly verify the effectiveness of selectively gating the orthogonal deviation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph-based social recommendation combines interaction and social graphs to model preferences under sparse feedback.
Mismatched social ties can contaminate representations and reduce model robustness.
Existing methods mainly prune, rewire, or weight social edges, but a single connection weight cannot selectively suppress misaligned message components.
ODSR decomposes social messages into aligned and orthogonal components, gates the deviation dimension-wise, and adds contrastive regularization.
The authors report improvements over strong baselines on three datasets and supporting analyses of selective deviation gating.

source_observation.claim: A social neighbor may share some interests with a target user while differing on others.

interpretation.claim: Social information may need component-level control rather than uniform connection-level scaling.

application.claim: For recommendation systems with heterogeneous social signals, consider representation-level or dimension-wise gating of potentially misaligned information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether dimension-wise gating is beneficial beyond the reported social recommendation setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three datasets, baseline identities, or quantitative performance differences.
The abstract does not describe the ranking-supervision formulation or contrastive-regularizer details.
